whyItMatters: Diverticula are acquired pouches of mucosa and submucosa pushed out through weak points where vessels enter the wall. They are most common in the sigmoid and can lead to diverticulitis, abscess, perforation, and bleeding.
treatment: Uncomplicated diverticulosis may be managed with a high fibre diet. Complications may need IV antibiotics, guided drainage, or surgery such as Hartmann's procedure.

findings: Anteroposterior projection of the abdomen and pelvis
Double-contrast barium enema study with air and barium visible throughout the large bowel
The ascending colon and transverse colon demonstrate smooth, well-distended haustral folds with uniform barium coating and no mucosal irregularity

The descending colon and sigmoid colon demonstrate numerous small rounded and lobulated filling defects of varying size (2–10 mm range) projecting into the lumen, consistent with multiple polypoid lesions
The sigmoid colon shows the highest density of these filling defects, with a carpeting pattern of polyps
The rectum appears distended with barium; a rounded soft-tissue density is seen in the pelvis overlying the rectal region, possibly representing a balloon catheter tip or pelvic soft tissue structure
Bony pelvis and visible lumbar spine show no acute osseous abnormality
No free intraperitoneal air is identified
No definite annular or apple-core constricting lesion is identified on this view
differential: Familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP): The innumerable small polyps carpeting the left colon and sigmoid are the dominant feature, and the pattern of hundreds of adenomatous polyps is classic for FAP
Attenuated FAP or MYH-associated polyposis: A lesser polyp burden variant that may appear identical on imaging
Hyperplastic/serrated polyposis syndrome: Multiple hyperplastic or serrated polyps could produce a similar radiographic appearance, though less commonly this numerous
anatomyConcerns: The right colon and cecum are not clearly visualized in the field; adequate filling of the cecum cannot be confirmed from this image alone, representing a potential study incompleteness
The rounded pelvic density overlying the rectum could represent a retention catheter balloon, an overlying structure, or a pelvic mass — superimposition limits characterization
Significant asymmetry in polyp distribution (left-sided predominance) is noted; this could reflect true anatomical distribution or incomplete mixing/coating of barium on the right side
